reviews.text: This restaurant was truly full of surprises! The signature dish, braised pork belly, had just the right amount of fat but wasn't greasy and melted in your mouth, and the side dishes were also perfectly cooked. The waiters were friendly and quick in service, and even carefully recommended new seasonal menu items. The elegant atmosphere with soft lighting was perfect for a small gathering with friends. The downside is that it gets quite crowded on weekends, so I think reservations are essential. The price is a little high, but the portions are generous, so it's good value for money. I especially recommend the plum juice, it is refreshing and delicious. Overall, it exceeded my expectations and I have already recommended it to my colleagues. I plan to visit with my family next week. I think it would have been better if there were more seats in the waiting area. In short, it was one of the most satisfying dining experiences I've had in a while, and I'll definitely be back!

The service is impeccable. However, the restaurant atmosphere is somewhat ordinary. The interior is simple and has no particularly eye-catching design elements. The price is reasonable, making it excellent value for money. Overall, this will be a very satisfying dining experience for those who value food quality and service. The atmosphere may not be fancy, but the delicious food and excellent service make up for it. Highly recommended for a friends gathering or family meal.

reviews.author: 首尔外围Outcall&Incall
reviews.text: Overall, this restaurant was a satisfactory experience. The staff was friendly, served food quickly, filled our water and plates first, and responded quickly to our requests. The atmosphere was simple yet elegant thanks to soft lighting and appropriate seating spacing, and it didn't feel crowded or noisy. The price was reasonable, and the portions were generous, making it good value for money. However, we recommend making a reservation as there may be a waiting time during peak hours. Window seats have a great view and are perfect for gatherings with friends. The cleanliness of the store was excellent, and the tableware was also clean. There was ample parking space in the basement of the mall, which was convenient. The matcha ice cream dessert was also really delicious. reviews.text:
Insa-dong, which runs from 63 Insa-dong, Jongno-gu, Seoul to 136 Gwanhun-dong, is a relatively narrow street of 700m in length. The road was formed along a stream that started from Samcheong-dong, passed through Gwanhun-dong and Insa-dong, and reached Gwangtong Bridge where it meets Cheonggyecheon Stream. During the Japanese colonial period, the stores here, along with those in Myeong-dong and Chungmuro, became a window for the exploitation of cultural assets.

In the 1920s, art and cultural property stores that developed mainly in Chungmuro ​​and Myeong-dong began to move to Insa-dong, where rents were relatively low, in the 1960s, which became an opportunity for Insa-dong to develop in earnest. Afterwards, a street was formed where merchants from nearby areas, including Nakwon Market, gathered, and in particular, many shops related to art gathered, and art galleries and cosmetics stores became the mainstay.

As there were many related shops, an exhibition hall naturally opened here, and it continues to this day, forming a cultural street. Nowadays, there are a variety of traditional Korean culture shops, including traditional tea houses, art galleries, art tool shops, traditional restaurants, and pottery shops. The government also fostered cultural streets, and in 1988, Insa-dong was designated as a ‘traditional cultural street’ and various cultural events and festivals are being held there.

However, this is not the only Korean culture store. There are also foreign franchises that can be found anywhere, but what stands out is that they try to fit in with the atmosphere of Insa-dong. A foreign coffee shop is the only one in the country to display its signboard in Korean in Insa-dong, highlighting its Korean image.

Insadong Cultural Street: A place full of the scent of Korean tradition
Insadong is not just a street. It is a treasure trove of culture where Korean tradition and art are alive and breathing, and is a must-see for tourists visiting Seoul. This place, where the history and cultural heritage dating back to the Joseon Dynasty remain intact, is a special space where you can enjoy the beauty of Korea while walking along the alleys.

A street steeped in history and culture
Insa-dong is the site of Dohwaseo during the Joseon Dynasty, and was formed as a collective residence for artists. Afterwards, antique stores, art galleries, and craft shops opened, naturally establishing itself as a center of traditional culture. In particular, since the 1988 Seoul Olympics, it was designated as a 'street of traditional culture' and more and more people are visiting it.

Various attractions and experiences
In Insa-dong, you can spend leisurely time sipping fragrant tea at a traditional tea house, and enjoy shopping while looking at various crafts. Additionally, you will have the opportunity to develop your artistic sensibility by experiencing traditional Korean paper making or appreciating Korean paintings. Various exhibitions are held in small art museums and galleries hidden in every alley, making it a great space for art lovers.

Famous places in Korea loved by people around the world
Insa-dong is a representative cultural tourist destination in Korea and is very popular among foreign tourists. Anyone who wants to feel the traditional beauty of Korea should visit this place at least once. In particular, Ssamziegil in Insa-dong is a place where you can see the works of various individual artists, and is popular among young people.

A living cultural space that is constantly changing
Insa-dong is not simply a space that preserves the past, but a living cultural space that embraces the present and the future. Tradition and modernity are harmoniously combined to create a new culture, which is constantly changing through the activities of young artists.

Why you should visit Insadong
Experience Korean traditional culture: You can directly experience various cultures of Korea, including Hanok, traditional crafts, and tea culture.
Appreciating works of art: You can develop your artistic sensibility by appreciating the works on display at various art museums and galleries.
Make special memories: You can make unforgettable memories by walking through the alleys of Insadong.
Shopping: You can purchase a wide variety of souvenirs and gifts.

conclusion
Insadong is not just a tourist destination, but a cultural space deeply connected to our lives. Enjoy the beauty of Korea and create your own special memories in this place where the past, present, and future coexist.

[Tips]
You can explore more leisurely if you visit on a weekday rather than a weekend.
Visit Ssamziegil in Insa-dong and admire various works of art.
It's also a good idea to relax while drinking tea at a traditional teahouse.
Explore the small shops hidden in the alleys.

Those of you who have watched Korean dramas will be familiar with Pojangmacha, or Pocha for short. A pojangmacha is a tent restaurant where people order food and drinks, confide in friends, or bond over a drink. Since my travel companions had never eaten at a pocha, I decided to have dinner at a pocha.

There are many Pocha Streets, but the most famous is Pocha Street above Jongno 3-ga Station. If you go before 6pm, there may not be any empty seats on the street, so look around and find a place you like.

We ordered stir-fried chicken gizzard, stir-fried pork cartilage, grilled ginkgo nuts, chive pancake, dumplings (dumplings with minced meat and mung bean vermicelli), egg rolls, and raw octopus. It was quite a generous portion for four people, but I wanted to let my friends try all the must-try dishes at Pocha.

Stir-fried pork cartilage and stir-fried chicken gizzard were really delicious! The rest was okay, but not wow-worthy. The highlight of dinner was the raw octopus. The octopus came out with its legs wiggling around, and it was really delicious! Pick up a piece, dip it in the sauce, put it in your mouth, and chew it. The faster you chew, the faster the octopus will stop moving. There is nothing fresher than this, and it tastes as if it was just caught from the sea.

The total damage was 138,000 won. The price is not cheap. And they only accept cash. After dinner, take a walk around this neighborhood. It used to be a place that sold guitars and other musical instruments, but now there are almost no musical instrument stores left.

reviews.author: 産閑
reviews.text:
In mid-December, when your mind gets more complicated as the end of the year approaches, Changdeokgung Palace is a good place to take a moment to catch your breath. Although it is located in the middle of Jongno, Seoul, this palace makes you feel like the flow of time slows down the moment you enter the walls. Especially if you go on a weekday morning, there are very few visitors, so you can enjoy the relaxation as if you are renting a palace.

Arrive around 9 a.m., buy a 3,000 won admission ticket, and immediately pass through Donhwamun to see the quiet scenery unique to the Winter Palace. It is a time when you can hear the sound of stepping on gravel and the wind passing through tree branches louder than the noise of people, so you forget for a moment that you are in the city.

The first thing you come across is Injeongjeon, which is impressive with its large yard and neat dancheong, as it is the place where the king of the Joseon Dynasty held official ceremonies. As December's shallow winter sunlight falls diagonally on the building, the colors subside calmly rather than being exaggerated. The atmosphere felt on site is much calmer than what you see in photos.

As you pass Injeongjeon and walk along the daily spaces of the king and queen, including Seonjeongjeon, Huijeongdang, and Daejojeon, the aesthetics of Changdeokgung Palace's architecture are clearly revealed. There are elegant buildings with well-proportioned and well-structured structures rather than flashy buildings, which fit well with the winter season. Even if the scenery is not covered with snow, the atmosphere of the winter palace is vivid enough with just the light and shadows.

A little further in, Nakseonjae and Seokbokheon have a quieter atmosphere. Perhaps because it was a private space where later kings stayed, there are fewer people and the tranquility is maintained. The combination of red wooden windows, grey-brown tiles, and fallen leaves remaining on the floor is like looking at an ink painting. This is a good section for organizing complex thoughts.

It takes about 40 minutes to walk around the palace, and it is a leisurely route even if you walk slowly and take pictures in between. Changdeokgung Palace in mid-December is not as crowded as it is during the fall foliage season, and it is a time when you can enjoy the plain winter scenery before the snow piles up, so it is especially suitable for “people who want to walk quietly.”

Rather than going too far away at the end of the year, it is a good idea to take a day off on a weekday and take a leisurely walk around Changdeokgung Palace. Instead of crowded cafes, the experience of walking alone through the grounds of a 600-year-old royal palace is one of the quietest luxuries you can enjoy in winter in Seoul.

reviews.author: Joseph Lee
reviews.text: After King Taejong Lee Bang-won ascended to the throne after killing his brothers, he was reluctant to see the deaths of his relatives and did not want to be in Gyeongbokgung Palace, which had a large official residence and showed his private life, so the narrow space and neatly built palace across from him is Changdeokgung Palace. After Gyeongbokgung Palace was burned down during the Japanese invasions of Korea, the kings of Joseon mainly lived in Changdeokgung Palace and did a lot of business there. Although Gyeongbokgung Palace and Deoksugung Palace suffered hardships during the Japanese occupation, with their pavilions being torn down and torn down, Changdeokgung Palace was spared from such damage because it was the residence of King Sunjong of the royal family. However, a botanical garden and a zoo were built there, and after a fire broke out in 1920, it was restored again and the interior was decorated in a splendid style like Deoksugung Palace. Touring the pavilion costs 3,000 won. The door leading to another pavilion is narrow and the chin is small, so be careful as you may hit your forehead or head. reviews.text:
Norakdang is the largest and most central building in Unhyeon Palace. The overall shape is a ruler, and the three front compartments have open front thighs, and one of the two compartments between the left and right sides is open and serves as a passage for the left wing. The 2 rooms on each side are ondol, and the 3 rooms in the center are daecheong. The wings on the left and right, that is, the part bent at a right angle from the main building, had two protrusions each and were used as a kitchen and warehouse. Norakdang is a seven-story building, and many of the architectural techniques of the nobility can be seen, and beautiful patterns on the bars remain.

The south haenggak to the south of Norakdang has a ruler-shaped plan, forming a ruler-shaped courtyard together with Norakdang, which has a ruler-shaped plan. This is the place where Empress Myeongseong, Queen Min, received queen training after completing her three royal weddings, and the wedding ceremony between King Gojong and Empress Myeongseong, held in the 3rd year of King Gojong's reign.

I went to see a musical reenacting Myo Hyeol Lye at Yeong nyeong Jein Hall and recommend it.
The period is from 24.4.27. to 24.5.1, and is held twice a day at 13:00 and 16:00.
It is free to visit, with no separate admission fee other than the 1,000 won admission fee to the National Palace. Tickets can be reserved in advance online and on-site on a first-come, first-served basis.
Those who pre-order online also receive a flower & bird tray as a gift.
Seats are not reserved, but are on a first-come, first-served basis.
Hats are given out for free, but it's a good idea to bring a parasol as well.
After the performance, you can take pictures with the actors, but only 15 teams are allowed, so if you want to take pictures, please run and stand in line. The line is on the left side facing the stage, so it is best to sit on the left side.
Have fun watching everyone~^^
